audit_findings.title: The valuation date is post-acquisition, but both the earnings claim and balance-sheet bridge are pre-acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $560.0 million acquisition funded with $530.0 million of new borrowings; replaces $31.975 million annual base rent plus percentage rent
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes equity-level OE through terminated rent, new interest, depreciation, taxes, insurance and maintenance capex; also changes the balance-sheet bridge and asset perimeter
audit_findings.evidence: The annual base rent is $ 32,225,000 in 2025 and $ 31,975,000 in 2026 with the lease term expiring at December 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated cutoff error. The September 6, 2026 valuation describes a post-July 1 common-equity claim using June 30 debt, cash and investments and a 2025 OE anchor. The $530 million borrowing is large relative to the modeled equity values of $1.117-$1.439 billion, while the acquired properties materially change recurring costs and capital requirements. Direction is mixed because rent disappears and owned real estate is added, but interest and maintenance obligations also arise.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the bridge from the first post-closing balance sheet and rerun all scenarios using pro-forma equity OE that removes NHI rent and incorporates interest, depreciation, taxes, insurance and normalized maintenance capex for the acquired properties.

audit_findings.title: Restricted insurance assets may have been added to equity without the claims they secure
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum identified bridge exposure $68.2 million, or $4.16 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially overstates the stakes_net bridge add-on by treating encumbered insurance assets as distributable investments
audit_findings.evidence: Restricted cash and cash equivalents and restricted marketable securities represent assets that are primarily held by our wholly owned limited purpose insurance companies for workers' compensation and professional liability claims.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether restricted assets entered stakes_net is unresolved. Nevertheless, the questioned component cannot exceed the entire $68.2 million add-on. Removing all of it would reduce base value from $79.39 to about $75.23 per share and bull value from $87.89 to about $83.73, still far below the $218.64 price. It therefore cannot change the supplied valuation conclusion, although the bridge should still be documented.
audit_findings.action: Provide a security-level reconciliation of stakes_net and cash_and_sti, identifying restricted status, claim reserves, regulatory capital and deferred taxes; remove any restricted amount included without demonstrable surplus.

audit_findings.title: Actual capital expenditure may understate sustainable maintenance needs
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated maintenance-capex deduction inflates anchor OE and every scenario derived from it
audit_findings.evidence: We are undertaking a process to allocate more aggressive capital spending within our owned and leased facilities in an effort to address issues that arise in connection with an aging physical plant.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization possibility, not a demonstrated calculation error. The filing states that more aggressive spending is needed for an aging physical plant, while FY2025 property additions were $36.446 million and the July 2026 transaction converted 35 leased facilities into owned assets. The record does not separate maintenance, growth and deferred modernization spending, so it cannot establish the sustainable deduction or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Build a facility-level maintenance-capex schedule for existing and acquired properties, separate growth projects and catch-up modernization, then rerun OE and all valuation scenarios using the normalized recurring amount.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring land-contribution gain may remain in the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.606 million pretax; approximately $2.723 million after the filed 24.5% tax rate; approximately $2.34 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: If unremoved, the nonrecurring gain inflates the $84.9 million OE anchor and its discounted operating value
audit_findings.evidence: The gain has been included as a reduction of “other operating expenses” in the consolidated financial statement of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE remains unresolved because the supplied OE reconciliation is absent. Even assuming the full after-tax gain remained, proportional recomputation reduces base value by about $2.34 per share, from $79.39 to roughly $77.05, versus a $218.64 market price. That scale does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation and confirm that the $3.606 million gain and only its associated tax effect were removed exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Declining supplemental Medicaid relief may be treated as permanent earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.246 million FY2025 revenue; approximately $5.471 million after the filed 24.5% tax rate; approximately $4.69 per base-case share if eliminated permanently
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration without matched cost relief would lower normalized OE and the growth path derived from the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.evidence: We have recorded $ 7,246,000 , $ 12,749,000 and $ 20,214,000 in net patient revenues for these supplemental Medicaid payments for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The revenue and its 2023-2025 decline are demonstrated, but future expiration is unresolved; first-half 2026 payments of $3.605 million were close to $3.684 million in first-half 2025. Even the conservative assumption that all FY2025 payments disappear permanently, with no matched expense reduction, lowers computed base value from $79.39 to about $74.70 per share and remains far below the $218.64 price. It does not change the supplied conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm each state program's legal duration and expected 2026-plus payments, identify specifically matched expenses, and normalize revenue and expenses together in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow adjustments may not match the common-share claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scale indicators are $2.591 million of 2025 income attributable to noncontrolling interests and $5.754 million of noncontrolling equity at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Unallocated consolidated depreciation add-backs or capex deductions could cause OE to include cash flows belonging to minority owners
audit_findings.evidence: The Company owns 65% of the operations entity and owns 89% of the real estate entity.
audit_findings.explanation: The allocation mismatch is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error. Its apparent perimeter is small: 2025 noncontrolling income was 3.1% of the $84.9 million OE anchor, and June 2026 noncontrolling equity was about 0.5% of total equity. Those concrete scale indicators, together with the supplied deterministic test finding only a small gap, make a conclusion-changing effect unreasonable on the current record, although the exact cash-flow mismatch remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile depreciation, amortization, capex and other OE adjustments by subsidiary and ownership percentage, and remove the portions attributable to minority owners.
